title: Tenant Geo-lock Enforcement and Proofstream
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-focused geo-lock enforcement mechanism for the Hosted API that ensures requests and persisted data conform to customer-specified region constraints, plus an automated proofstream that bundles routing/retention evidence for audits. This ticket covers product acceptance criteria, UX flows for the Console and API, rollout plan with fallbacks, and the exported artifact format required by compliance teams.
background: Enterprise customers with strict sovereignty requirements have asked for tighter guarantees than soft region preference: they need a mode that (1) prevents cross-region persistence and (2) produces cryptographically verifiable evidence showing where traffic and derived artifacts were stored and for how long. Existing work covers residency manifests and region pin operators; this work ties those primitives into a tenant-facing enforcement workflow and a proof export pipeline that can be consumed by compliance teams and legal auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Tenant can opt into 'Geo-lock (Strict)' mode and select allowed regions via a guided wizard.
API: Requests to the Hosted API include a tenant residency header and are rejected with 403 when routed outside allowed regions under Geo-lock mode.
Runtime: Smart-router respects geo-lock at routing time and will not fall back to incompatible regions; when capacity constraints occur, requests receive a deterministic error with remediation hints.
Evidence: System produces an 'audit bundle' (signed ZIP) containing routing logs, storage locations, retention settings, and policy decisions for a configurable time range.
Export format: Audit bundle follows JSON-lines for events and includes a manifest with hash digests; format documented in Confluence design doc.
Telemetry: New metrics for "geo_lock_violations", "geo_lock_reject_rate", and per-tenant proof bundle generation latency are emitted and wired to the Console dashboard.
Rollout: Feature gated and enabled progressively by percentage for pilot tenants; migrations documented and rollback path validated.
Security: KMS/HSM signing of proof bundles or equivalent verifiable signature integrated and confirmed by Security review.
Tests: End-to-end e2e tests simulate multi-region failure modes and validate audit bundle content against a canonical fixture.
Docs: Console help text, API spec, and compliance-runbook updated.
Support: Runbook and alerting for failed export generation and customer-impacting rejects created.
Legal: Evidence package format approved by Legal for typical audit requests.
ux_notes: Wizard: Stepper that asks for regions, retention profile, and a soft-fallback policy. If user selects 'Strict', UI surfaces explanation that requests will be rejected rather than diverted.
Default: For new tenants, Geo-lock is off; include a 'check impact' simulator that shows expected reject rate based on historical traffic for selected regions.
Bulk change: Admins can apply geo-lock profiles to multiple tenants; UI confirms impact before applying.
Evidence UX: Allow immediate on-demand 'Generate Proof Bundle' and scheduled daily bundles retained for customer-configured windows.
Tooltips: Explain what is included in the proof bundle (routing logs, storage locations, policy version, signed manifest).
api_contract: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/residency -> sets residency profile (regions list, retention_policy, enforcement_mode)
Header: X-Redwood-Tenant-Residency required when enforcement_mode=strict; server returns 403 if mismatched.
GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/proof-bundles?from=&to=&format=jsonl -> returns presigned link to signed ZIP
Webhook: Optional webhook subscription for 'proof-bundle-ready' events with bundle URL.
Error semantics: 409 when profile conflicts with reserved infra; 503 when no compatible capacity in allowed regions (with structured remediation payload).
implementation_notes: Smart-router: Add a strict-routing path that validates allowed regions for tenant at decision time and marks requests for rejection if incompatible.
KV cache considerations: Ensure cached responses don't violate geo-lock by tagging cache entries with region origin and tenant residency profile.
Evidence pipeline: Stream routing + storage events into a compact JSON-lines sink (partitioned by tenant) with periodic signer job that bundles and signs artifacts.
Storage: Use per-tenant object prefixes and server-side encryption with customer KMS keys where requested.
Retention: Integrate proof bundle retention settings with existing retention operator and retention audit logs.
Operational costs: Proof bundle generation may be IO-heavy; budget initial quota and rate limit generation per tenant to avoid S3 cost spikes.
Fallback policy UX: For 'Strict' mode customer must be explicitly warned about potential 403s; offer an intermediate 'Preferred' mode that attempts compatible regions then fails gracefully.
Backward compatibility: Existing tenants with prior residency manifests should be auto-mapped into the new profile but remain in 'Preferred' unless they opt-in to 'Strict' via explicit consent flow.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Pilot): Enable for 3 invited pilot tenants. Smoke tests + manual verification of proof bundles. (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Gradual): 10% rollout to tenants with low throughput; monitor geo_lock_reject_rate and proof bundle generation errors (3 weeks)
Phase 2 (GA): Full self-serve release with billing and support docs; default mode remains 'Preferred' to avoid accidental outages (2 weeks)
Rollback: Feature flag to disable strict routing globally and regenerate scheduled proof bundles if necessary.
Migration window: Provide a migration assistant in Console that runs impact simulation and requires explicit confirmation before upgrading tenant to 'Strict'.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High reject rates causing customer outage when Strict mode misconfigured. Mitigation: Simulator + mandatory double-confirmation + release gating.
Risk: Proof bundles missing critical fields. Mitigation: Schema-driven e2e tests and signed manifest schema with required fields; legal sign-off required before GA.
Risk: Cost spike from large historical proof requests. Mitigation: Rate limits, quotas, and staged export generation with cost alerts.
Risk: KV cache serving stale region-tagged entries. Mitigation: Invalidate cache on residency profile changes and add region metadata to cache keys.
open_questions: Should proof bundles be signed with tenant-managed keys (customer KMS) or Redwood-managed keys? Security prefers tenant keys but adds UX friction.
What is the canonical retention policy for proof bundles (default 365 days?) and how does that interact with customers who need longer retention?
How should we expose per-request region provenance in logs without creating PII or inflating log volumes?
Do we want to allow per-route overrides (e.g., allow embeddings to be computed outside region but stored inside)? This complicates enforcement semantics.
